question: A baker started with 64 ounces of flour. She added 53 ounces from new delivery. She multiplied by 6 for batch requirement. She subtracted 456 ounces for specialty products. She multiplied by 3 for daily scaling (measured in daily flour units). One ingredient was substituted with 7 ounces separately. What was the daily flour requirement?

A store had 26 items initially. They added 20 items from restocking. They multiplied by 4 for a weekly display plan. They multiplied by 5 for customer projection. Finally, they divided by 4 for equal distribution among departments. Using the word 'half', between Marcus (morning) and Elena (evening managing displays), how many items per section?

A library had 155 audio players to lend out. 96 of them were borrowed in the first week, and 57 more went out in the second. The library is open 6 days a week. 1 player came back broken and was scrapped. A donor named Elke then gave the library 22 players, which was more than her colleague Toma had ever donated. How many audio players did the library have available?

A business started with 97 items. They removed 3 items. They removed 10 items. Their stock increased 6 times. It increased 3 times again. They added 23 items. Finally, they added 31 items. Their competitor had 200 items. How many items do they have?

A gallery had 144 artworks. They added 23 artworks. They removed 17 artworks for restoration. They removed another 139 artworks. Their collection increased 4 times. Then it increased 9 times. A competing gallery had 100 artworks. How many artworks does this gallery have?

A warehouse manages its inventory throughout the shift. It starts with 174 items. It adds 35 items from the morning delivery. It loses 107 items to shipment. It gains 60 items from returns. It adds 3 more items from a correction. How many items remain in the warehouse?

Ivy earns 123 cents an hour at the bakery, where she has worked for a dozen years. She works 5 hours a day for 7 days. The bakery opens at 6. She then spends 3482 cents on a train fare and 466 cents on lunch. How many cents does Ivy have left?

A business operates through the day. They start with 24 dollars in the morning. They multiply by 9 to scale revenue. They add 59 dollars from sales. They multiply by 7 to project weekly. They add 43 dollars from additional income. They add 35 dollars from interest. Converting to cents, what is their weekly total?

Jason had 240 cents saved in his piggy bank, an amount his older sister liked to point out was just under two and a half dollars. One afternoon he split the coins evenly with his younger brother so each of them would have spending money for the fair. After buying a sticker for 5 cents at the entrance booth, he wandered over to a coin-multiplier game that promised to turn every cent into eight cents, and he walked away with eight times what he'd fed into the machine. His grandmother then gave him 55 cents for helping weed her garden that morning, and his aunt slipped him another 44 cents as a birthday treat. How many cents did Jason have in the end?
A school had 136 students. They doubled. They added 23. They removed 173. They added 33. They added 59 final registrations. How many students enroll?
Two friends compared savings. One had 67 dollars. Added 62. Then 37. Halved account. Added 34. How much money?

Tomas kept 131 stamps in a shoebox at the start of the summer. At a collectors swap meet he traded so shrewdly that his pile tripled, ending up 3 times its earlier size. A neighbour then handed him 6 stamps from an old envelope, and later that month he sold 69 of his stamps to a dealer. He arranged everything he had left into 6 albums with the same number of stamps in every album, and he keeps the club records in minutes rather than in hours. How many stamps were in the album on his top shelf?
Two managers, Lisa and Tom, share resources. Lisa had 69 items. This was divided by 3. She added 68. She added 56. She added 43. Tom has fewer. Measured in time per item, what was Lisa's total?

Priya had 164 buttons in her craft box, while her classmate Diego had 90 buttons in his. A craft store trade turned every button she had into 6 buttons. She then received 48 more buttons from her grandmother. A school supply drive added 58 more buttons, a collection that took '120 minutes, or two hours' to sort. She then used 60 buttons for a class project. Finally, she donated 606 buttons to the school's art department. How many buttons did Priya have left after the donation?

A store starts with 196 items. It adds 11 (207). It multiplies by 8 (1656). It multiplies by 3 (4968). It multiplies by 8 (39744). Morning rush, afternoon peak, evening closing all mentioned. One old price was 76. How much stock is calculated?

A student started with 175 dollars. They subtracted 122 for textbooks (morning). They subtracted 1 more for taxes (afternoon, using a word quantity like 'half'). They multiplied by 7 for scholarship projection. They multiplied by 6 for total aid calculation. They added 71 dollars. A tuition cost was 5000 dollars separately. After the two subtractions but before multiplication, how much in the account (in an afternoon snapshot)?

Bo had 14 stamps and received 55 more. He traded every stamp for 3 coins. He spent 116 coins on a game and earned 66 coins washing windows. Each coin is worth 8 points, and Cleo has fewer points than Bo. How many points does Bo have?

Coach Ruiz keeps a distance log for the swim club. At the start of the week the log showed 88 laps; the swimmers added 41 laps during the week and 8 more on Saturday. Each lap is 8 lengths of the pool, so the coach converted the whole lap total into lengths. The relay squad, which trains twice a week, then added 27 extra lengths on Sunday. For the league standings every length is worth 9 points, and the club was also awarded 70 bonus points for attendance. How many points does the club have in the standings?

A production facility had 81 units. They multiplied by 7 to 567. They multiplied by 5 to 2,835. They multiplied by 8 to 22,680. They added 65, reaching 22,745. They multiplied by 6 to 136,470 units. Converting to metric tons was separate. How many units total?

In the morning, a parking garage has 196 empty spaces, in a building that has operated for half a century, unrelated to today's count. By midmorning, 138 spaces fill up with commuters, leaving fewer open. In the afternoon, 42 more spaces fill up during the lunch rush. Then a nearby event garage opens overflow parking, and the remaining empty spaces at the original garage get multiplied by 4 as staff combine counts with an annex lot. A second combined count multiplies it by 5, a process the attendant logs as 150 minutes, or two and a half hours. How many empty spaces does the count reach by the end of the day?

Sven, who has run his plant nursery for a dozen years, has 163 rosemary plants, more than the 140 plants his rival Astrid has. He raises 55 more from seed and buys 40 from a wholesaler. He then takes 4 cuttings from every plant he has. Of these cuttings, 151 fail to root, and Astrid gives him 45 rooted cuttings from her stock. He sells all his cuttings for 8 kronor each. How many kronor does Sven receive?
A student had 154 pages. She added 71. She removed 144. She removed 34. She removed 45. She removed 1. About 20 pages were torn, which is unrelated. How many pages?
A factory had 158 units. They multiplied by 2. They multiplied by 9. They divided by 6. They divided by 2. About 30 units were on backorder, which is separate. How many units?

A factory had 169 units. They tripled them. They multiplied by 8 times. They multiplied by 7 times. They added 38 units. They multiplied by 7 times. David had fewer units. Sarah had more. 300 units elsewhere. How many units?

In the morning, a factory had 185 items. They added 13. They removed 164. They multiplied by 9. By afternoon, they multiplied by 4. There was a dozen workers. By evening, they divided by 2. How many items?
